# Chapter 2: Number systems

<!-- BEGIN HEADER (generated by tools/build.py) -->
> [Home](../../../../README.md) › [Part I — Computer Science Foundations](../../index.md) › [1. Computer Fundamentals](../index.md) › Chapter 2: Number systems

- **Status:** Drafted · 10 syllabus topics
<!-- END HEADER -->

A computer is a physical machine, and the only thing a physical circuit can reliably distinguish is a small number of states. Everything else (integers, fractions, text, pictures) is built from sequences of those states. This chapter shows how numbers are written in positional systems, how to convert between systems, how arithmetic works on binary numbers, how negative numbers are represented, and how fractional values are approximated with floating point.

The chapter is mathematical in places, but each idea is introduced with a concrete picture first, and every algorithm is shown as runnable code with output you can compare with your own.

Read the lessons in order. Each one uses ideas from the one before it.
